subject: Post-demo follow-up: latency / throughput probe plan + next tests
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah@nimble.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nimble AI Procurement <procurement@nimble.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Redwood latency & throughput specifics

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team found Redwood's routing/fallback story compelling. A couple of follow-ups from internal engineering and procurement: 1) can you share p95/p99 latency numbers and sustained tokens/sec (streaming and non-streaming) for the 3 sequence lengths we discussed (64, 512, 2048) running the LlamaX-13B equivalent model? We want to baseline Redwood vs our current hyperscaler endpoints. 2) do you have a short A/B test plan we can run on our side (or you run) that isolates batching, quantization, and KV cache effects? 3) procurement noted we'd need an initial SLA draft and an attachment with test evidence (CSV or raw logs) to move to an internal technical review.

High level asks: p95/p99 numbers, tokens/sec sustained, short A/B plan, and any sample results you can share quickly. Would appreciate a short triage plan (who owns which test) and a 7–10 day runway to validate.

—Sarah
Sarah Lin
Head of Platform, Nimble AI

Attachments: none
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@nimble.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Redwood latency & throughput specifics

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear asks and for hosting the demo. Quick recap and proposed next steps below.

Recap (from our side):
- Goal: apples-to-apples comparison vs your hyperscaler endpoints on p95/p99 latency and sustained tokens/sec for LlamaX-13B-equivalent.
- Key variables: sequence length (64/512/2048), batching policy (no-batch / 16-concurrency batching / dynamic batching), quantization (fp16 / int8), KV cache enabled/disabled, and streaming vs non-streaming APIs.

Proposed division of work (7–10 day runway):
1) Redwood will run an initial probe across sequence lengths with our standard model variant (13B fp16) to produce a p95/p99 + tokens/sec CSV and raw latency histograms. Owner: Marcus. Target: initial CSV within 48 hours.
2) Nimble to run an A/B probe against your hyperscaler endpoints using our probe config (attached). If you prefer, we can run both and share raw logs for you to validate. Owner: Sarah / Nimble eng.
3) Engineering deep dives: run three controlled A/Bs isolating (a) batching, (b) quantization, (c) KV cache. We'll provide the exact command-lines and seed inputs. Owner: Karthik + Marcus.
4) Commercial: draft SLA and sample billing estimate for committed throughput; we'll include an SLA-draft attachment. Owner: Jordan.

Initial target metrics we aim to collect (for each config):
- p95 latency (ms)
- p99 latency (ms)
- median latency (ms)
- sustained tokens/sec (non-streaming, measured as tokens completed per second under sustained load)
- burst tokens/sec (tokens accepted/sec under 30s spike)
- CPU/GPU utilization and memory tail (percentiles)

I'll attach our probe config and a minimal example of the CSV schema we will use. Marcus — can you confirm you can run the probe within 48 hours and include: raw histograms, CSV, and a short notes file describing test harness (tooling, seed prompts, and environment)?

Sarah — if Nimble prefers Redwood to run both sides to reduce variance, say so and we'll include a short signed test plan and a shared S3 bucket for logs.

Proposed follow-up meeting: Thu Apr 8 10:00 AM PT to review initial CSVs and agree on A/B specifics. If that works I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_probe_config.yaml (probe commands + env)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Sarah Lin <sarah@nimble.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Redwood latency & throughput specifics

On Mon, Apr 5, 2027 at 12:03 PM Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear asks and for hosting the demo. Quick recap and proposed next steps below.

Following up with the test plan specifics and an early-run preview. I ran a short internal probe against LlamaX-13B-equivalent (Redwood-13b-fp16) on our staging dedicated pool to validate the harness. Summary first, then exact commands and samples attached.

Quick results (staging, single-worker, no quantization, KV cache disabled):
- seq=64: p95 38ms, p99 82ms, sustained tokens/sec (non-streaming) ~ 1,250 tps
- seq=512: p95 120ms, p99 220ms, sustained tokens/sec ~ 430 tps
- seq=2048: p95 640ms, p99 1,200ms, sustained tokens/sec ~ 110 tps
Notes: these are from a 5-minute steady-state run with 50 concurrent requesters using the redwood-prober tool. We measured both streaming and non-streaming; streaming tail latencies were ~10–15% higher in p99 due to chunking overhead.

What I'll attach (all in drive link):
- redwood_vs_hyperscaler_probe-configs-20270405.yaml (probe script + arguments used)
- redwood_vs_hyperscaler-results-sample.csv (CSV with columns: config, seq_len, batch_mode, quant, kv_cache, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, tps_non_stream, tps_stream, gpu_util)
- raw_histograms.tgz (compressed latency histograms)

Next tests we propose (A/B isolations):
A) Batching impact: compare no-batch vs dynamic batch (target batch_size=8/16) at fixed concurrency to show throughput vs tail.
B) Quantization impact: fp16 vs int8 (with identical prompt seeds). Track change to p99 and p95 and any quality delta (we'll provide a small eval set).
C) KV cache: cold vs warmed KV cache for multi-turn flows (measure p95 p99 over sequence of 8 turns).
D) Network pathing: run identical probe from Nimble's region vs our Hosted region to measure egress/ingress variability and routing fallbacks.

Operational asks for Nimble if you run probes: provide a sample curl or prober invocation to your hyperscaler endpoint and the credentials to run 24–48 hour test (short-lived token works). If you want Redwood to run it, we will need a signed test plan + S3/Drive write access.

I'll upload the initial CSV and the raw histograms to the Drive link and send a short gist with the redwood-prober command-lines.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior SW Eng, Performance — Redwood Inference
